issues: Sense 3_pw: dropped gloss term. German {%Grenze des Landes und der See, Gestade, Küste, Ufer,%} lists four members, Russian {%Граница суши и моря, побережье, берег,%} lists only three — 'Ufer' is unrendered. (Sense 2 correctly maps the shorter PWG list Gestade, Küste -> побережье, берег 2:2, so this is a PW-only synonym falling out.) Fix: render all four, e.g. {%Граница суши и моря, побережье, взморье, берег,%}.

Sense 1: interpolated verb not present in the German. {%Zeichen, welche die bestimmten Punkte%} -> {%знаки, которые (определяют) определенные пункты%}. The German fragment is deliberately verb-less (the governing verb falls past the masked span {T20}); the Russian supplies '(определяют)'. It is honestly bracketed, so severity is low, but it asserts a relation the source does not state at that point. Fix: drop the parenthetical ({%знаки, которые определенные пункты%}) or mark the addition with editorial square brackets.

ADVISORY (non-blocking), 3rd block tag 4: German '4〉 {%reden —, sprechen über%} ({T181})' collapses to Russian '{%говорить о%}' — the reden/sprechen doublet is reduced to one verb, whereas the same doublet is rendered 'говорить, разговаривать' at tags 16/18/28. Suggest 'говорить, разговаривать о' for consistency.

ADVISORY, 1st block tag 1: '{%Jmd%} ({T54}) {%anreden, mit Jmd sprechen%}' → '{%кого-л.%} ({T54}) {%обращаться, говорить с кем-л.%}' — the accusative 'кого-л.' cannot govern with 'обращаться' (which takes к + dat.); the parallel sense (3rd block tag 3) gets it right as 'обращаться к кому-л., говорить с кем-л.'. Align the two.

ADVISORY, consistency: the same German lemma 'Gerede' is rendered 'толки' at tag 10 but 'речь' inside 'Gerede, gesprochene Worte' at tags 1/13/16. Pick one equivalent for the entry (both are defensible in isolation; 'толки' is the closer match for 'Gerede').

ADVISORY, segmentation only (no meaning change), 3rd block tags 14 and 17 (and mildly 15): German's two-span frame '{%Jmd%} ({T190}) {%erwiedern%}' / '{%Etwas%} ({T193}) {%besprechen%}' is merged into a single Russian span with the case-marking parenthetical pushed to the end, so the masked case abbreviation no longer sits adjacent to the argument it governs. All {Tn} are preserved; only the alignment of gloss-span to case marker shifts.

ADVISORY, tags 5 and 11: 'sprachen zu einander' / 'zu einander sprechen' → 'говорили друг другу' / 'говорить друг другу' (dative, implying 'said to each other <something>'); 'говорить друг с другом' renders the German more exactly — the collision with 'mit einander plaudern' → 'болтать друг с другом' is already avoided by the different verb.

Sense 1, editorial frame: German "Das {T55} als {T56} an Stelle des {T57} {T58}:" opens a headed noun phrase with the definite article; Russian "Это {T55} как {T56} вместо {T57} {T58}:" converts the article into a demonstrative pronoun ("this"), which Russian does not require. Idiomatic scholarly form drops it: "{T55} как {T56} вместо {T57} {T58}:". Non-blocking — no meaning added or lost, but the demonstrative is an insertion.

Sense 1, terminology: "mit nicht vorgeschobenem Tone" → "с непродвинутым ударением". The sense (accent not shifted forward) is conveyed, but "продвинутое ударение" is not the received Russian term; "с непередвинутым (вперёд) ударением" / "без переноса ударения вперёд" is the standard philological register. Non-blocking.
